rows.verified: HSE groups agricultural-machinery safety around safe use, risk assessment, design, maintenance, farm vehicles and mechanical hazards.
The Safe Stop procedure requires the handbrake to be engaged, controls placed in neutral, power switched off and the key removed or power locked off.
Safe Stop should be followed before leaving the operating position and before maintenance, adjustment or blockage-clearing work.
Before use, the machine should be suitable for the job and its guards and safety devices should be fitted and working.
Machine operators, including casual and seasonal workers, should be trained and understand the relevant instructions and risk information.
Pre-use checks should cover defects such as brakes, wheels and tyres, as well as guards, emergency stops and controls.
Guards and safety devices must not be removed, defeated or bypassed to speed work or deal with blockages.
Before clearing a blockage, falling or rotating parts and stored spring or hydraulic energy must be secured or released safely.
Agricultural-machinery risk depends on machine type, guarding, maintenance, task, terrain, operator competence, bystanders and operating conditions.
HSE machinery guidance is machine-, task-, operator-, site-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Occupational-asthma symptoms can include wheezing, coughing, chest tightness and severe shortness of breath.
Symptoms may occur immediately after workplace exposure or several hours later, which can obscure the occupational link.
Occupational asthma can be an allergic reaction to respiratory sensitisers such as flour or wood dust.
Once the lungs become hypersensitive, further exposure to a sensitiser at relatively low levels may trigger an attack.
COSHH requires employers to assess and control exposure to hazardous substances that can cause occupational asthma.
Employers should consider substituting harmful products with less harmful alternatives where practicable.
Exposure controls such as local exhaust ventilation, protective equipment, supervision and operating instructions must be kept effective.
Workers exposed or likely to be exposed to an asthmagen should receive suitable health surveillance for early detection.
Occupational-asthma risk depends on sensitiser, concentration, exposure route, duration, controls, susceptibility and health-surveillance timing.
HSE asthma evidence is substance-, workplace-, worker-, exposure-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
